articleTitle: Enhanced Privacy Setup for Blockchain-Enable IoT Devices Using Multi-Factor Authentication
abstract: As the number of Internet of Things (IoT) devices keeps growing, security has become a major concern. With trade-offs like complexity and scalability, maintaining privacy in the system is a highly desired characteristic. This work presents an architecture for the management of IoT devices with Hyperledger Fabric. We incorporated our system with blockchain and Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) surveillance camera at a rental property. When new renters arrive, the CCTV security camera automatically reroutes its stream. We implemented multi-factor authentication via push notifications and web tokens to enhance security between renters and property owners. One of our contributions is an effective architectural framework that makes use of multi-factor authentication and key invalidation circumstances. Our proposed scheme enhances the security of IoT devices with blockchain technology and mitigates the risk of a single point of failure, providing a robust and reliable solution.

articleTitle: Improve the Applicability of Trinocular Stereo Camera in Navigation and Obstacle Avoidance
abstract: This study proposes an obstacle avoidance method based on a trinocular system, enhancing performance in multi-obstacle environments through depth sensing and point cloud processing, significantly improving stability and accuracy. The results show that the trinocular system offers high reliability and superior navigation performance in complex scenes, providing valuable insights for autonomous navigation technologies.

articleTitle: Enhancing Road Safety: A Pedestrian-to-Vehicle Collision Warning System Integrating Location-Based P2P and LiDAR Sensing
abstract: Pedestrian-to-vehicle collisions pose a significant risk in modern traffic environments. This paper presents a collision warning system that integrates a location-based peer-to-peer (P2P) network with LiDAR sensing technology to enhance road safety. By incorporating road users detected by LiDAR as virtual peers, the system enables the visualization of both connected and non-networked users on mobile applications. Field experiments confirmed that the proposed system effectively detects and displays road users, providing timely collision warnings. These results highlight the system's potential to improve pedestrian and vehicle safety through innovative integration of P2P and LiDAR technologies.

articleTitle: Near-Field Channel Estimation for OFDM Extremely Large-Scale Array Systems
abstract: The concept of extremely large-scale arrays (XL-arrays) is gaining significant attention for future 6G networks, thanks to their potential to deliver numerous advantages. To fully leverage the capabilities of XL-array systems, accurate channel state information (CSI) is essential. In this context, the near-field effect plays a crucial role. A near-field channel is characterized by both angles and distances, known as polar parameters. In OFDM systems, the channel is also influenced by delays. This paper proposes a channel estimation method that takes advantage of full geometric sparsity within a hybrid combining architecture. We begin by investigating polar sparsity, followed by an examination of delay sparsity. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Study on the Detection of the Gingival Region Using Oral and Dental Spectral Image Database (ODSI-DB)
abstract: Periodontal disease is an infection in the mouth caused by periodontal disease bacteria and is known as a dangerous disease that can eventually cause teeth to fall out. Early detection of periodontal disease is important because there are almost no subjective symptoms in the early stages of periodontal disease. Conventional diagnosis of periodontal disease is mainly done by probing examinations by doctors, and research on automatic diagnosis using images has been delayed. In recent years, automatic diagnosis technology using hyperspectral images has been attracting attention in the medical field, and many research results using the Oral and Dental Spectral Image Database (ODSI-DB) have been published. Recent research results suggest the possibility of detecting the disease by gingival imaging, and we aim to establish a method for extracting gingival sites by combining Mask R-CNN and U-Net. It was clarified that the proposed method can detect marginal gingiva around the tooth almost accurately.

articleTitle: Loop Bandwidth Extension Technique for FVF -Based Low Drop-Out Regulator
abstract: This paper proposes an output capacitor-free analog low-dropout regulator (LDO) suitable for memory circuits. The circuit architecture adopts a flipped voltage follower (FVF) configuration. The local loop incorporates super source follower (SSF) and gain boosting stage (GBS) circuits to extend loop bandwidth and enhance loop gain. This LDO is implemented in a 90nm process. In simulation result, with an input voltage of 1.05V, it maintains an output voltage of 1V and supports output load currents ranging from 100uA to 40mA. Under load switching conditions with a load step time of 10ns, the undershoot voltage is 140mV, settling time is 550ns, and quiescent current under heavy load conditions is 45uA.

articleTitle: Development of Cutaneous Feedback Haptic Glove for VR Industrial Training
abstract: Traditional industrial training methods often require extensive time, cost, and resources for effective preparation and execution. This paper presents a virtual reality (VR)-based solution for industrial training, enhanced by a cutaneous feedback haptic glove that improves the immersive learning experience. The developed haptic glove integrates a high-resolution tactile pin array that provides realistic feedback through the fingertips, allowing users to sense interactions with virtual objects. The VR training environment, created using Unity, simulates a crane sorting system that replicates real-world industrial operations. This setup enables users to manipulate a virtual crane through hand motions, with the haptic glove delivering tactile feedback that enhances the sense of realism. This approach not only advances skill acquisition but also opens opportunities for safe and cost-effective training in complex industrial tasks. By leveraging VR and cutaneous feedback, this study contributes to the modernization of training methods, reducing risks associated with real-world training scenarios and offering a pathway toward more immersive, effective industrial training.

articleTitle: The Application of a Deep Learning Image Recognition Model Based on Multi-Scale Convolutional Attention Mechanism for Clinical Open Wound Detection
abstract: Wound detection is essential for preoperative evaluations and postoperative monitoring in clinical settings. This study presents a deep learning-based image recognition model that uses a multi-scale convolutional attention mecha-nism for automatic wound detection and classification, along with a depth estimation model to assess wound healing. Featuring 1,449 clinically annotated wound images, the model combines YOLOv8, for instance, segmentation with SegNext for en-hanced spatial attention, achieving a detection mAP50 of 0.885 and a classification mAP50 of 0.801. The ArUco Marker-based method allows for precise wound area estimation with an error margin of less than 0.6%.

articleTitle: 3rd Crystal Oscillator in BJT Architecture Using Negative-Capacitance Circuits
abstract: This paper proposed a 3rd harmonic crystal oscillator that implemented in a BJT architecture with voltage loop tuning. The design integrated Negative Capacitance Field Effect Transistors (NCFETs) into the base circuit of the 3rd harmonic oscillator. The two ends of the negative capacitance are connected to the base and collector of the BJT element in the circuit, respectively, thereby improving noise performance and stability. The proposed design utilized TSMC's 0.18-micron process to obtain the physical chip, and validation and analysis are then performed using an SSA signal source analyzer. The phase noise is -156dBc at 1Mhz and the RMS jitter is 158.47 fsec. The result shows that the BJT architecture with NCFETs can achieve notable results in oscillator architecture.

articleTitle: Investigation of Table and Graph File Creation Tool Using Physical Block and AR Technology
abstract: DX (Digital Transformation) will be promoted through paper digitization and web conferencing. The AR (Augmented Reality) numerical table and graph creation tool in Microsoft Excel using NyARToolKit for Unity is suggested. It can display the numerical table and graph from the AR figure block and output it to Excel files. After that, we investigate the effect of the AR numerical table and graph creation tool to compare the PC use and AR figure block operation.

articleTitle: Multi-Object Tracking for Animals with Evolutionary Computation Based Optimization
abstract: To analyze animal navigation, tracking of animals is important. The fish tracking challenge is a newly introduced challenge that aims to accurately detect ten fish and track them. For that purpose, the SweetFish dataset was provided. To develop a tracking system of fish, we finetune an object detector on SweetFish dataset to detect fish bounding boxes, because a pre-trained object detector cannot accurately find animals. For tracking, deep-learning based tracker was used and their parameters were automatically optimized by evolutionary computation, because re-identification cannot be used for fish detection and it is necessary to optimize hyperparameters for this case.

articleTitle: Error-Rate Improvement via SVD-Based Reduced-Stream Transmission for MIMO and Large-Scale MIMO Systems
abstract: In this paper, we propose and discuss a new spatial-multiplexing scheme designed to better exploit the potential of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channels for improved error- rate performance. Specifically, we utilize singular value decomposition (SVD) to select only the “good“ parts of the channel for transmission. The modulation order is increased to maintain the same transmission rate and ensure a fair compari-son. Our findings are then extended to large-scale MIMO systems, where both the precoder and detector are constructed using the hybrid analog/digital architecture to reduce the implementation complexity. Simulation results demonstrate that, given a specific transmission rate, our proposed methods generally outperform conventional spatial-multiplexing approaches regarding the over-all error-rate performance.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Fall Prediction System Using Neural Network Algorithms on a Microcontroller
abstract: Based on the needs of hospital rehabilitation centers, this study focuses on posture detection for patients undergoing rehabilitation in hospitals, especially the elderly. The goal is to ensure that nearby medical staff receive alerts as soon as possible when a potential fall is detected, allowing them to intervene before an incident occurs. This paper proposes a fall prediction system that uses sensor fusion and a Feedforward Neural Network (FNN). The system consists of a Bluetooth-enabled microcontroller unit (MCU) integrated with a 6-axis Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU), which is placed on the patient's collar. In this study, the potential movements performed by patients during rehabilitation are classified into nine categories: standing, stomping, stair climbing, stretching, waist twisting, bending over, squatting, walking, and running. Motion data from the IMU is processed using an FNN and k-means clustering for movement classification and abnormal motion detection. If a potential fall is detected, an alarm is sent via Bluetooth to notify nearby medical staff. Finally, the proposed fall prediction system will be implemented on a Bluetooth-enabled MCU module.

articleTitle: Channel-Hopping Sequences with Flexible Channel Labeling for Cognitive Radio Wireless Networks
abstract: Channel-hopping (CH) protocols are essential in modern cognitive radio (CR) technology, as they facilitate rendezvous between secondary users (SUs) and improve spectrum efficiency by enabling dynamic access to limited spectral resources. Traditional CH protocols rely on a global-labeling framework, assuming that all SUs share the same mapping scheme from logical channels in their CH sequences to physical frequencies in their CR transceivers. However, when SUs operate in different regions or encounter varying frequency availability, this framework can lead to mismatches in channel-to-frequency mappings, hindering effective channel rendezvous. This paper proposes two construction algorithms for asynchronous universal-labeling (UL) CH sequences that adapt flexibly to both global and autonomous labeling scenarios. Simulation and numerical analyses demonstrate that the proposed UL CH sequences achieve an optimal balance of maximum rendezvous diversity, even channel utilization, and minimal maximum time-to-rendezvous, thereby enhancing spectrum flexibility and efficiency in CR wireless networks.

articleTitle: Fast Inter Prediction Encoding Based on Occupancy Map in V-PCC
abstract: In Video-based Point Cloud Compression (V-PCC), the point cloud system converts the input 3D image into multiple 2D images to represent the original data. These 2D images include a geometry map, a texture map, and an occupancy map. The occupancy map consists only of binary values, 0 and 1, to indicate whether a pixel value exists at a specific location in the input 3D point cloud data. Currently, the High-Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) codec, designed for natural image compression and decompression, is used in this process. However, the occupancy map's characteristics cannot be fully leveraged within HEVC. In this paper, we propose a fast inter-prediction method that takes advantage of the binary nature of the occupancy map, consisting solely of 0s and 1s. During inter-prediction in HEVC, the codec evaluates multiple Coding Unit (CU) sizes to find the one with the lowest Rate-Distortion cost(RDcost). Our proposed algorithm enables the encoder to utilize the current occupancy map values to determine the best encoding mode for the CU block dynamically. This enables early termination of inter-prediction, leading to a significant reduction in overall encoding time. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach, achieving an encoding time reduction of up to 11.43%, thereby improving the overall efficiency of the encoding process.

articleTitle: ECU s Fingerprint Identification Based on CAN Bus Using 1D-CNN
abstract: Traditional Electronic Control Units (ECUs) fingerprinting classification methods for Controller Area Network (CAN) systems rely on manually defined features such as maximum voltage and average voltage, requiring a large number of features to effectively distinguish between different ECUs. However, these methods often face challenges in scalability and generalization across diverse environments. This study addresses these issues by adopting a one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN) model with automatic feature extraction capabilities, significantly reducing the reliance on manual feature engineering. The model features a short training cycle and fast inference speed, making it highly suitable for real-time applications in resource-constrained environments. Experimental results demonstrate that the model achieves a classification accuracy of 99.98%. Moreover, this approach shows great potential for deployment on embedded platforms and adaptability to dynamic operating conditions, paving the way for future advancements in vehicle security systems.

articleTitle: Sensorless Power Measurement for Personal Computers Using CMOS MEMS Magnetometers and Machine Learning
abstract: We present a novel, sensorless power meter for accurate and real-time power estimation of personal computers (PCs). Our innovative system integrates CMOS MEMS magnetic field sensors with machine learning-based IoT analysis, allowing power consumption to be measured without traditional sensors. At the core of our device is a CMOS MEMS search coil magnetometer, fabricated using the TSMC 1P6M 180nm process and calibrated against a commercial power meter. Coupled with Python software that monitors GPU utilization, CPU usage, and two temperature metrics, we developed a multivariate nonlinear regression (MNR) model with 59 terms to predict power consumption. After an initial training phase, our system can measure the power consumption of any PC sensorlessly, achieving less than a 2.95% discrepancy in average power measurements over 20 minutes. This scalable approach facilitates deployment across multiple PCs or servers in data centers, enabling real-time power reporting and carbon footprint calculations. By efficiently monitoring power usage in diverse computing environments, our method significantly enhances energy management and sustainability efforts.

articleTitle: Implementation of Multi-Level RAG Model for Enhanced Synergistic Vulnerability Analysis
abstract: Traditional vulnerability analysis models often rely on a single data source, which limits their ability to comprehensively detect and analyze vulnerabilities. In this study, we propose a multi-level Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) model that progressively integrates multiple vulnerability databases to overcome these limitations. By incorporating core and peripheral data sources at different levels, our approach aims to enhance the quality of vulnerability analysis. We integrate four major vulnerability databases-National Vulnerability Database, CERT Vulnerability Notes Database, GitHub Advisory Database, and Exploit Database-into a Level 4 RAG model. This integration demonstrates an average performance improvement of 6.4% compared to a Level 1 model that only refers to the National Vulnerability Database. The evaluation is based on several metrics, including METEOR, BERT Score, Faithfulness, and Answer Relevancy, which collectively highlight the benefits of a multi-source, incremental integration strategy for more effective vulnerability analysis. These results highlight the potential of multi-level RAG models in enhancing vulnerability analysis through the integration of complementary vulnerability data sources.

articleTitle: A Broadband Millimeter-Wave 5G Front-End Module IC in 22nm CMOS FD-SOI
abstract: In this paper, we present a broadband millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) 5G front-end module (FEM) integrated circuit (IC) designed in an advanced 22 nm CMOS FD-SOI (Fully-Depleted Silicon-On-Insulator) process offered by GlobalFoundries (GF). The broadband mm-Wave 5G RF (radio-frequency) FEM IC includes a broadband power amplifiers (PA), a low-noise-amplifier (LNA), and a SPDT (single-pole double-throw) switch. The performance of the FEM IC is simulated with post-layout parasitic extraction (PEX) and compared vs. available measured data. This work suggests an all-silicon RF FEM IC may be attractive for some commercial mm-Wave 5G and 6G applications.

articleTitle: A 10-Bit Successive Approximation Register Analog to Digital Converter Using VCO-Based Time-Domain Comparator
abstract: The successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) architecture is employed to achieve low power consumption, allowing it to operate at low supply voltage. A time-domain quantization architecture based on a time-domain comparator is combined to overcome the design bottlenecks caused by the reduced intrinsic gain of transistors, the increased process variation, and the decreased supply voltage in advanced processes. A voltage-to-time converter based on a voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) is used, providing the benefits of circuit stability and low noise impact. This design can be further improved by adding an SR time amplifier to the output of VCO, allowing the phase difference to grow exponentially. Hence, a faster escape from the dead zone of the phase detector can be realized to resolve the issue between high resolution and high speed in traditional VCO comparators. To accommodate the output generated by the improved voltage-to-time converter, the operation mode of the phase detector is modified, enabling it to be applied to the new voltage-to-time converter output. This paper presents a 10-bit SAR ADC in TSMC 40nm process, with a conversion rate of 10MS/s, a supply voltage of 0.9V, power consumption of 57.9µW, an ENOB of 9.88 bits, an SFDR of 74.07dB, and a FoM of 6.14 fJ/conv.-step.

articleTitle: A High-Reliability Transmission Mechanism for Data Acquisition in Smart Sensing Applications
abstract: Smart sensing applications span a diverse range of industries and domains, utilizing advanced sensor technologies and data-driven methodologies to monitor, analyze, and automate various processes. To enhance transmission reliability, particularly in dynamic and unpredictable environments, the use of redundant data transmission is commonly employed. However, to address challenges related to energy efficiency and fairness, it is essential to manage and constrain the transmission of redundant data in a controlled manner. In this paper, we propose a novel transmission mechanism designed for data acquisition in smart sensing applications. Numerical analysis demonstrates the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed mechanism in such applications.

articleTitle: Efficient Sharing of Computing Environments According to Their Use-Urgency by Using Containers Over P2P Network
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method for efficiently sharing various computing environments among multiple users using containers. In this method, container images and caches, which are intermediate products of builds, are stored as digital content in a hybrid P2P network and shared among users. Each user can retrieve images and caches through index servers according to the demands of his or her computing environments, and use the desired computing environments. By adjusting the type of content to be retrieved according to the urgency of the environments required by each user, the content items can be efficiently stored and shared within the network. In addition, these content items are reallocated in the network according to the demands of all users periodically. The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated using computer simulations.

articleTitle: From Pharmacy to Home: A Medication Management System to Overcome the Digital Divide for the Elderly
abstract: The average lifespan in Taiwan has increased to 79.84 years, leading to an aging society where 88.7% of the elderly have at least one chronic disease, and 51.3% have more than three. Medication adherence is crucial for managing these conditions, but the national adherence rate is only about 50%. Taiwan's robust medical system allows patients to receive a 28-day supply of medication through health insurance. However, elderly individuals living alone often struggle with timely medication use, leading to wasted resources and deteriorating health. Existing medication management products lack digital functions and networking capabilities, resulting in poor outcomes. This study integrated the pharmacy's drug administration process with a smart pill box mechanism to improve medication adherence. The system uses IoT technology and sensing components to provide real-time monitoring and reminders. The smart pill box reads a QR code on the medication package to set reminders and connect to the internet. A trial with 142 users showed that over 95% found the system helpful, and about 90% believed it could improve medication quality. As technology advances, such systems will become increasingly important in addressing the challenges of an aging population and a shortage of healthcare workers.

articleTitle: A DTN-Based Wireless Sensor Network for Small-Scale Industry
abstract: This paper designs a wireless sensor networks (WSNs) system for small-scale industries, utilizing Delay/Disruption Tolerant Network (DTN) technology for sensor data gathering. Our system consists of a sensor node, a relay node and a sink, and gathers sensor data to the sink using the Store-Carry-Forward (SCF) method. In addition, to address the delays for data gathering from the sensor node to the sink caused by the SCF method, our system introduces a function to estimate the data acquisition time based on the times that the sensor and relay nodes retain sensor data in their memory. Furthermore, we have developed a prototype system and verified its effectiveness through performance evaluation in an actual environment. As a result, we have confirmed that the introduction of SCF improves reliability by 37.3%.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Approach to Food Image Aesthetic Assessment via Structural and Color-Based Feature Integration
abstract: Assessing the aesthetic quality of food images requires capturing both structural and color-related attributes, a task that poses significant challenges. This study introduces a hybrid approach that integrates deep features of the VGG-16 model with RGB color histograms, providing a representation of the aesthetics of food image. Deep features capture structural and textural details, while RGB histograms highlight color-related attributes such as brightness, harmony, and balance. Our experimental results on a public dataset demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art performance, surpassing baseline methods. The method maintains a balance between precision and recall across aesthetic labels, ensuring robust evaluation. Furthermore, the study underscores the complementary role of RGB color histograms in enriching deep feature representations, showcasing their synergy in enhancing overall performance. The effectiveness of SVM in managing high-dimensional feature spaces is also validated, reinforcing its suitability for aesthetic assessment tasks.

articleTitle: Implementation of Broadband Sine Wave Current Power Supply by Using GaN Device
abstract: This paper utilizes the fast-switching characteristics of Gallium Nitride (GaN) devices to design a broadband low harmonic sine wave power converter capable of modulating a stable sine wave current from 10 mHz to 30 kHz. The system further adopts a three-phase interleaved synchronous buck converter architecture, with a switching frequency reaching 1 MHz, effectively enhancing the inductor current characteristics and significantly reducing the inductor ripple current. Finally, by measuring the small signal ac voltage and current of a lithium-ion battery, the impedance magnitude and phase at a given frequency can be derived based on Ohm's law, thereby enabling real-time online electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurement.

articleTitle: Vehicle Tracking Using Lane Cameras for Personalized Parking Guidance
abstract: Real-time monitoring of vehicle movements within a parking lot is crucial for creating a personalized parking guidance service. This applied research proposes using lane cameras to monitor vehicle dynamics, employing YOLOv8-based license plate object tracking and character recognition to determine the real-time location and movement direction of vehicles, while achieving cross-camera object tracking capabilities. With this critical information, the parking management system can provide tailored parking guidance instructions for each vehicle, reducing the burden on drivers to locate available parking spaces and contributing to lower carbon emissions.

articleTitle: Edge Optimization Algorithm for Geometry Maps in AV1-Enabled V-PCC
abstract: Point cloud is a three-dimensional data representation based on points and is widely applied in the field of 3D vision technology to describe the geometry of objects or scenes. They serve as a crucial data storage format. However, due to the large volume of point cloud data, compression techniques are essential for reducing its size. To address this, the Moving Picture Experts Group (MPEG) developed the Video-based Point Cloud Compression (V-PCC) process specifically for dynamic point cloud data, utilizing High-Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) as the encoder. Despite these advancements, point cloud compression often results in the loss of edge points, which leads to the formation of holes, the appearance of compression artifacts, and a subsequent degradation in visual quality. This study employs the AOMedia Video 1 (AV1) encoder for point cloud compression and introduces an effective method to mitigate compression artifacts. By leveraging the characteristics of occupancy maps generated during the V-PCC process, this study identify the edges between patches in 2D projected point cloud images from different projection angles by a distance transform algorithm. Along these edges, distortion values in the geometry maps before and after compression are recorded, and pixels with significant distortion are compensated. The optimized geometry map is then re-encoded by AV1 and further processed through the V-PCC decoding workflow, ultimately producing a higher-quality reconstructed point cloud. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an average improvement of 2.63% and 2.12% in point-to-point and point-to-plane MSE, respectively. Furthermore, in terms of BD-rate results, the compression efficiency for point-to-point and point-to-plane PSNR improves by an average of -3.0% and -2.2%, respectively, thereby further enhancing the subjective visual quality of the reconstructed point cloud.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Desktop Application Capable of Sharing Images with Smartphones and PC
abstract: We have opportunities to share images in our daily lives, and there are a variety of methods used for image sharing, including cloud-mediated, server-mediated, and direct communication between terminals. Since there is no standard way to share images directly between Windows and iOS, this study will prototype an application that enables this direct sharing between them. It is also desirable that image files be communicated through a secure communication channel because they contain personal information. As a fulfillment of this requirement, this study utilizes the WebRTC mechanism and implements a desktop application using BLE. This study enables image sharing between Windows and iOS.

articleTitle: Obstacle Detection and Collision Avoidance from Blind Spots in Self-driving Wheelchair*
abstract: This study aims to develop a cost-effective autonomous electric wheelchair equipped with an early-stage obstacle avoidance system to handle blind spots at intersections, ensuring safe mobility for elderly users. In Japan, the demand for electric wheelchairs is rapidly increasing, with approximately 20,000 units shipped annually, driven by the progression of a super-aged society. Meanwhile, traffic accidents remain a significant issue, particularly at intersections where incidents involving elderly drivers are on the rise. Although previous studies have proposed collision avoidance systems for autonomous vehicles and electric wheelchairs, the unique challenges of wheelchair autonomy, including the economic feasibility of advanced sensors and the distinct risk scenarios at intersections, remain unresolved. To address these issues, this research focuses on the development of a practical solution to improve safety and mobility for the growing population of elderly electric wheelchair users.

articleTitle: C-Element-Based Latch for Flip-Flops: Complete SNU and Partial DNU Tolerance and Resilience to Soft Errors Around Clock Edges
abstract: As semiconductor device dimensions and operating voltages continue to scale, soft errors from high-energy cosmic rays pose significant reliability challenges to microelectronic systems. This paper presents a C-element-based latch design for constructing master-slave flip-flops. HSPICE simulations using a 15 nm process design kit demonstrate that connecting the output node of the latch to the input of the next C-element achieves complete Single Node Upset (SNU) tolerance and enhanced Double Node Upset (DNU) tolerance. Experimental results show that while most nodes remain stable under DNU conditions, certain configurations may still experience data flipping. Additionally, excessive charge accumulation at C-element output nodes affects input signals. However, connecting the output to the next C-element input significantly increases the critical charge threshold. Furthermore, the latch and its flip-flop exhibit complete SNU tolerance at input nodes around clock edges.

articleTitle: Impact of Nonorthogonal Code Shift Keying in Power Line Communication Environment
abstract: This study examines the performance of a CDMA system utilizing multi-valued code modulation in Power Line Communication (PLC) environments. Specifically, Code Shift Keying (CSK) with nonorthogonal codes is employed as the multi-valued code modulation technique. The proposed CSK scheme aims to achieve higher transmission efficiency compared to conventional CDMA systems. Analytical evaluations and numerical results are provided to validate the potential of the proposed CSK method in PLC scenarios.

articleTitle: Latent Space Denoising Model for High-Precision 3D Cardiac Model Generation
abstract: This study introduces a Latent Space Denoising Model for generating high-precision 3D cardiac models, tailored to assist in the diagnosis and treatment of cardiac-related diseases. By integrating patient-specific physiological data, medical imaging reports, and advanced Diffusion model techniques, the proposed method overcomes the limitations of traditional geometric reconstruction and image registration methods. The generated 3D models accurately preserve critical anatomical features such as the aortic root, valve junction, and aortic annulus, enabling enhanced preoperative evaluation and surgical planning. Experimental results demonstrate the model's ability to produce detailed and physiologically accurate cardiac structures, emphasizing its potential for clinical applications. The study lays the groundwork for further development and validation of 3D cardiac modeling technologies, with the ultimate goal of improving precision and outcomes in cardiac care.

articleTitle: Digital Twin System for Wireless Mesh Camera Node Placement Optimization of Japanese Small and Medium Sized Rivers Monitoring
abstract: In recent years, the risk of river flooding has increased in Japan due to the intensification of natural disasters, but river monitoring facilities have not been adequately developed for small and medium sized rivers. Wireless Mesh Camera Networks (WMCN) based on Wireless Mesh Networks (WMNs) are expected to be used in river monitoring of small and medium sized rivers. In this paper, we propose a digital twin system that optimizes the placement of camera nodes based on virtual reproduction of real environment topographic data around rivers and visualizes the results using PLATEAU data. Simulation results show that the proposed system can provides the river administrator with camera node placement considering the real environment.

articleTitle: Automatic Test Cases Generation Method by Structuring Specification Documents Using Seq2Seq
abstract: We aim to automate the development of communication software. By leveraging machine learning, we propose a method for automatically generating system testing test cases from requirement specification documents. In this research, we focus on developing a method to generate test cases by structuring requirement specification sentences using a deep learning Seq2Seq model with an Attention mechanism. Our goal is to further enhance the accuracy of this approach. To evaluate the effectiveness and characteristics of the proposed method, we conducted experiments using requirement specifications of communication system software and various IT system requirement specification documents.

articleTitle: Implementation and Evaluation of Digital Twin Using LiDAR and 3D City Models
abstract: Digital twins, which replicate real-world environments using data collected by devices and sensors, have garnered significant attention in recent years. These systems enable simulations of real-world conditions and predictions of future scenarios. To advance digital twin technologies, Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) has been promoting the development of 3D city models nationwide through Project PLATEAU. However, these models currently include only static objects, limiting their applicability for real-time simulations involving dynamic entities, such as those needed for traffic accident prediction. This paper proposes a method for constructing digital twins by integrating real-time pedestrian and vehicle data captured by LiDAR into 3D city models. The proposed approach, implemented using Unity, a widely used game engine, demonstrates its effectiveness in reflecting dynamic pedestrian and vehicle information in real time.

articleTitle: Seamless Switching Between Public and Non-Public 5G Network Using Smart Resource Flow Wireless Platform
abstract: In recent years, automated transportation systems have been used in factories to improve manufacturing efficiency. Trackless automated transportation systems require stable wireless communication for control and monitoring. In this system, equipment must move throughout a large factory area. In cases where outside building area is covered by a public 5G network and inside building area is covered by a non-public 5G network, a system is required to continue wireless communication seamlessly between the non-public 5G network and the public 5G network. We have developed the Smart Resource Flow (SRF) wireless platform to bundle and manage multiple wireless networks. We evaluated the impact of the SRF wireless platform on communication interruption when switching between public and non-public networks. From this evaluation, we confirmed that the communication interruption time was reduced from 9.75 s to 0.14 s by applying the SRF wireless platform.

articleTitle: Innovative Design and Application of the Digital Sustainability Cloud
abstract: This study addresses the challenges faced by Taiwan's manufacturing industry in carbon emissions data exchange and management, proposing an innovative solution. To meet the requirement of international policies such as the EU's CBAM and the U.S.'s CCA, businesses need more effective mechanisms to collect carbon emissions data across their supply chains. However, current challenges include inconsistent data formats, lack of a trusted data computation framework, disparities in digitalization among enterprises, and inadequate digital data sharing. To address these issues, this study adopts the PACT framework promoted by WBCSD, designing and implementing a carbon data exchange platform called the digital sustainability cloud, which complies with the Pathfinder standard. The platform is designed to protect supplier privacy with commercial consideration, leveraging innovative technologies to enable efficient and secure carbon data exchange. The platform has been successfully tested under PACT compliance and applied to the supply chains of 12 hub manufacturers, demonstrating its practicality and reliability. The primary contribution of this study is to provide a standardized platform architecture to address the carbon information exchange needs of the manufacturing sector. This architecture is not only applicable to Taiwan enterprises but can also be extended to international companies complying with PACT specifications. The proposed digital sustainability cloud is expected to serve as a critical tool for aligning carbon management in the manufacturing industry with international standards.

articleTitle: Revisiting Quantum Asymmetric Key Cryptography: Enhancing Practical Implementations with a Generalized Grover Search Algorithm
abstract: The quantum asymmetric key (QAE) cryptography scheme, originally proposed using the Grover quantum search algorithm and demonstrating significant advancements in theoretical generalization, is revisited. To enhance its practical implementation, the authors evaluate the protocol's performance under real-world conditions. This includes analyzing the impact of hardware limitations and the one-iteration Grover search algorithm (GSA) on QAE accuracy, with tests conducted on IBM Quantum simulators and devices. To address these challenges, the paper focuses on extending the GSA to support non-standard initial states. This is achieved by designing a tailored diffusion operator, resulting in the generalized GSA. The study marks the first practical implementation of QAE on IBM Quantum devices, introducing generalized GSA and providing empirical performance insights. Empirical results reveal scalability challenges, with success probabilities decreasing significantly as qubit count increases. For instance, the 2-qubit system achieves near-perfect accuracy, while the 4-qubit system shows notable degradation, especially on quantum hardware. These findings underscore the need for improved hardware fidelity and algorithmic optimization to advance quantum cryptography.

articleTitle: A Study of Guide Documentation for Introductory Flutter Programming Learning with Exercises
abstract: Dart is a programming language designed to facilitate cross-platform app development under Flutter environment. It has its own distinct format and structure that allow developers to write responsive codes while maintaining high performances across various platforms. Learning Flutter/Dart is easy for students who have been proficient in Object Oriented Programming (OOP) concepts in as Java, JavaScript, or C. However, as a new language for mobile cross-platform programming, Flutter/Dart has different features that must be understood. In this paper, we present a comprehensive guide documentation that outlines key elements and advantages of Flutter/Dart programming for its independent learning. It helps learners navigate through foundational knowledge and practical exercises. As next studies, we will complete the guide documentation to cover the features, make proper exercises to review it, and evaluate the proposal through applications to students.

articleTitle: XAI-Based Adaptive Feature Selection Method for Efficient Classification of Encrypted Malicious Traffic
abstract: As the number of devices connected to the network has increased exponentially, hyper-connected intelligent network environments have become common. As a result, as sensitive data transmission and reception become frequent on the network, encrypted traffic began to be actively studied for secure data communication. However, due to the nature of encrypted traffic, the number of cyber attackers bypassing detection systems, such as network intrusion detection systems (NIDS), and exploiting them to conceal attack behavior is on the rise. To address this, conventional detection methods—based on signal analysis, static and dynamic analysis, deep packet inspection (DPI), and artificial intelligence (AI)—are being studied. However, these methods face limitations in dealing with high-complexity mechanisms and are difficult to apply to zero-day attacks. In particular, AI-based detection methods, which have been extensively researched recently, suffer from low scalability and difficulties in explaining prediction results, making the reliability of the results uncertain. Therefore, this study proposes an enhanced principal component analysis (PCA)-based adaptive feature selection (AFS) technique to efficiently classify malicious encrypted traffic. AFS can strengthen detection performance by optimizing feature selection for learning and can demonstrate that the detection results for encrypted traffic are explainable, based on eXplainable AI (XAI).

articleTitle: Optimized Electromagnetic Parameters of a Six-Phase SPMSM with Fractional-Slot Concentrated Winding for Electric Vehicles
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) are widely utilized in a variety of applications due to their high efficiency, dependability, and exceptional dynamic performance. The increase in the number of phases of the PMSMs is a crucial step forward in improving the motor's overload and fault tolerance. Moreover, the PMSMs with outer rotor are extensively used in traction applications such as ship propulsion, mining, lifting, etc., due to their large torque density, which increases the ability to produce more torque. In this study, a unique optimal design technique with the goals of reducing material cost and boosting efficiency is proposed for a six-phase surface-mounted PMSM (SPMSM). Initially, an analytical model is developed to calculate main dimensions of a 145kW six-phase SPMSM. Next, an optimization process is presented to define optimal electromagnetic parameters of the proposed motor. Once optimal parameters are defined, a finite element approach is presented to simulate and analyze the electromagnetic parameters of the optimal motor. The obtained results after optimization are compared to the traditional motors After optimization, not only the material cost decreases 8USD and the efficiency increases 0.224 %, which achieve the objective functions, but also other output parameters such as back EMF THD, torque ripple, etc., of the optimal motor find better outcomes when compared to the initial model.

articleTitle: Maximum Likelihood-Based Angle Estimation for Movable Antenna Systems
abstract: Movable antenna (MA) is a new hardware capable of adjusting the position of an antenna to improve the communication performance. Precise estimation of angle in a MA system is important for its successful performance in data transmission. In this paper, maximum likelihood (ML)-based angle estimation technique for MA system is presented. Specifically, the likelihood function is formulated and angles that maximize the function is extracted. Numerical results demonstrate the proper estimation of angles.

articleTitle: Phishing Prevention Focusing on Certificates and Input Forms: PoC as Browser Extensions
abstract: Phishing attacks against consumers have become increasingly sophisticated, necessitating effective real-time detection methods. This study analyzes the characteristics of phishing sites, focusing on certificate validity periods and input forms. Based on a dataset of 1,047 unique fake website URLs collected from multiple sources, we found that 89.8% of the phishing sites had certificate validity periods of 90 days or less. To effectively prevent this threat, we developed a proof-of-concept (PoC) browser extension that leverages certificates and input forms as key indicators for real-time phishing detection. The PoC extension achieved an detection rate of 93.9%. Comparative analysis showed that our approach outperformed several existing solutions, including Google Safe Browsing, in detecting phishing sites. While the proposed method demonstrates high effectiveness, we also discuss its limitations. This study demonstrates the potential of approaches leveraging certificates and input forms for real-time detection, offering a simple yet effective countermeasure.

articleTitle: Selective Video Coding Method Using LCEVC and Base Codecs
abstract: This paper proposes a novel video coding method that selectively switches between Low Complexity Enhancement Video Coding (LCEVC) and a base codec at the Group of Pictures (GOP) level, leveraging the capabilities of LCEVC. LCEVC, which is standardized as MPEG-5 Part 2, is a cutting-edge video coding standard designed to enhance the efficiency of conventional codecs. However, due to its layered structure, there are cases where better video quality can be achieved without using LCEVC. To address this, the proposed method dynamically toggles the use of LCEVC, depending on the video coding results of each GOP. Experimental results show that this adaptive approach improves video quality by 16.18 % compared to LCEVC.

articleTitle: Implementation and Evaluation of Location-Based P2P System Using Geohash
abstract: In recent years, location-based services (LBS) have become increasingly prevalent. To facilitate direct communication between nearby devices using location information, a method called G-LocON (Geo-location Oriented Network) has been proposed. However, as the number of devices increases, server performance degradation becomes a significant issue. To address this, load balancing methods that employ additional servers have been proposed. Despite its advantages, this approach requires clear specifications for server configuration and management. Moreover, enabling collaboration among multiple servers is essential for scalability. This study proposes a server expansion and management method utilizing Geohash, a technique that converts location information into strings. Additionally, an implementation of G-LocON incorporating Geohash was developed, and its proper operation was successfully validated through experiments.

articleTitle: Time-Constrained Playlist Generation Using Text Embedding of Content Synopsis
abstract: This study proposes a playlist generation scheme that meets the requirement of time constraint. Playlist generation involves creating a personalized collection of audio/video contents and it plays a significant role in music and video streaming services. A personalized collection of contents automatically generated sequentially can be useful in on-demand streaming services during spare time; however, users may not be able to consume their desired suitable contents under limited time circumstances. To address this issue, we introduce a combinatorial optimization problem to meet a time constraint, namely the requirement that the total duration of the playlist is within the specified time length. The time-constraint optimization is formulated as a knapsack problem, which inevitably leads to an excessive computational burden for large-scale optimization. To reduce the high computational costs, candidate contents for the knapsack problem are narrowed down through a k-nearest neighbor search. An additional tuning parameter is incorporated to adjust the aggressiveness of selection depending on video duration, that is, prioritizing a specific range of video duration according to use cases. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed scheme realizes the playlist generation to meet the time constraint of total duration and policies for video duration priority.

articleTitle: Real-Time Cell Phone Recognition for Motorcycle Emission Inspection System
abstract: The impacts of air pollution on public health are becoming increasingly important. Taiwan has the highest proportion of mobile sources of pollution, which include automobiles, motorcycles, ships, and airplanes. These oil-fueled vehicles all emit pollutants that are harmful to humans, animals, plants, and the environment. The most direct way to reduce mobile pollution is through electric vehicles. The next approach is to require vehicles that have been in use for over five years to undergo regular emission inspections. However, many drivers often forget to perform regular emission inspections. Therefore, we propose an effective solution to improve vehicle emission inspection rates. Our system consists of three main components, the mobile application, the server-side system and the web interface. The system uses YOLOv8 on the mobile application for license plate recognition and STAR-Net to confirm license plate numbers. A web crawler is then employed to check whether the vehicle has undergone its regular emission inspection. The Cell phone test YOLOv8 model for license plate recognition with 95% accuracy, execution speed up to 22 to 30fps. The license plate numbers with 92% recognition rate using STAR-Net. The server-side system takes only 7 seconds from data reception to the completion of web crawling.

articleTitle: Formal Verification of Consumer Remote Sim Provisioning Common Mutual Authentication using BAN Logic
abstract: Remote Subscriber Identity Module (SIM) Provisioning (RSP) is revolutionizing cellular connectivity management in consumer mobile devices and Internet of Things (IoT) systems through over-the-air SIM profile downloads. This paper presents a formal security verification of the RSP Common Mutual Authentication protocol using Burrows-Abadi-Needham (BAN) logic. The analysis delves into the authentication procedure between the embedded Universal Integrated Circuit Card (eUICC) and the Subscription Manager Data Preparation+ (SM-DP+) server. By rigorously applying BAN logic principles, we show that the protocol meets its mutual authentication goals within stated security assumptions. While our verification confirms the protocol's mathematical correctness, we also identify potential vulnerabilities based on our findings and other relevant literature. This highlights the potential for improving the security architecture of RSP using emerging technologies like blockchain, cloud-based authentication proxies, and automated verification methods. These findings help to advance the development of strong security mechanisms for the increasing embedded SIM ecosystem.

articleTitle: OLSR-Based Route Construction Method that Locks the UAV in-Flight Link and Crossing Links
abstract: We have studied a method for constructing routes for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) using a multi-hop network of wireless devices installed in individual houses. To eliminate the risk of UAV collisions caused by overlapping routes when multiple UAVs are operating simultaneously, we propose a route-locking mechanism to prevent links in an established route from being reused in constructing routes for other UAVs. Additionally, we introduce a method to prevent the use of links that cross locked routes during the route construction process for other UAVs. We propose an OLSR-based route construction method that locks the links over which UAVs are flying and also locks the links that cross them. We evaluate its effectiveness through computer simulations.

articleTitle: Sound Localization Correction System Using User Position Tracking in Four Loudspeakers Environment
abstract: This paper implements a system that corrects sound localization in environments where four loudspeakers are installed and the user freely moves. Existing sound localization techniques in speaker environments assume an ideal relationship between the user and speaker positions. Thus, the sound image localization may become inaccurate when the user moves. In contrast, our system tracks the user's position in real time and automatically adjusts the sound volume and timing of each speaker based on the distance between the user and each speaker. By doing so, our system realizes accurate sound image localization regardless of the user movement. Furthermore, we verify the effectiveness of our system through user experiments.

articleTitle: Haptic Encoder and Data Compression of Multimodal Data Traffic in the Tactile Internet
abstract: The efficient transmission of haptic, audio, and video (HAV) data in the Tactile Internet (TI) is the bases for successful tele-operation services over long-rage area networks. The IEEE P1918.1.1 Working Group is going to standardize the encoding of haptic data in such networks. This study presents a first implementation of the haptic encoder that is in compliance with the future IEEE 1918.1.1 standard for non-delay transmissions. The encoder's details are outlined and the haptic encoding performance is discussed. In a basic leader-follower system configuration, a significant encoding gain at 44 % was observed when haptic devices are idle. Hence, a haptic tele-operation system can be realized with superior efficiency when haptic devices are in idle state, so that data traffic is optimized while reducing operational network costs.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation Based on Numerical Simulation of Novel Guided Spontaneous Emission Circuit for Improved Optical Power Resolution
abstract: We perform a numerical simulation to evaluate the performance of a guided spontaneous emission circuit aimed to significantly improve the optical power resolution (OPR). Experimental results suitably agree with numerical simulation results. The maximum slope, which is an improvement factor of the OPR, for forward and backward pumping are 9.5 and 4.4, respectively, at output wavelength of 1533 nm according to the experimental results. The maximum slope of forward pumping is more than twice the maximum slope value of backward pumping. In addition, a numerical simulation of the mode field diameter (MFD) dependence reveals that the maximum slope increases with increasing MFD and the largest maximum slope is 12.6 at the wavelength of 1533 nm.

articleTitle: Tiered Cache-HNSW: Using Hierarchical Caching System in HNSW
abstract: With the progress in generative AI technology, systems such as RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) are increasingly used. In these systems, graph-based Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search (ANNS) is commonly used for background information retrieval. However, as the size of the dataset increases, the search speed becomes significantly slower. In this paper, we propose Tiered Cache-HNSW (TC-HNSW) that caches pre-categorized datasets in layers. TC- HNSW prioritizes caching frequently accessed nodes into faster storage based on the number of accesses and their category, allowing faster searches. This paper describes TC- HNSW system design, caching strategy, and the efficiency of categorization-based caching. Our preliminary evaluation shows that categorization-based caching improves performance, achieving search speeds four times faster than traditional methods when search topics are specified.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Non-Linear Function Approximation for Transformer Deployment on Edge NPU
abstract: In recent years, Vision Transformers (ViTs) have outperformed Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in accuracy on computer vision tasks. However, deploying ViT models on edge neural processing units (NPUs) presents significant challenges, particularly in quantizing the model for integer arithmetic and efficiently supporting non-linear functions. While several previous works have quantized ViTs and their non-linear functions, they rely on division operations, which are costly on edge NPU implementations. Additionally, these approaches are non-all-integer or require fine-tuning (i.e., quantization-aware training, QAT) to restore accuracy, which takes at least 60 GPU hours on V100. This paper proposes a low-cost, integer-only, division-free approximation that requires no fine-tuning (i.e., post-training quantization, PTQ) for non-linear functions. We apply integer-only Softmax (IntSoftmax), integer-only LayerNorm (IntLay-erNorm), and Critical-Range-Aware Quantization (CRAQ) for GELU. Our method introduces only a 0.5% accuracy drop compared to state-of-the-art non-all-integer PTQ approaches across the DeiT series. Furthermore, we demonstrate the feasibility of our algorithm on an NPU that supports both CNN and Transformer models. Compared to prior works in NPU hardware design for transformers, we reduce LUT consumption by 70% and eliminate additional DSP overhead. These results highlight our algorithm's low-cost, efficient nature, making it suitable for edge NPU deployment.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Somatosensory Interactive Game with Sensor and Neural Network Integration
abstract: This paper presents an interactive motion-sensing game designed for ocean protection, aligned with the United Nations' 14th Sustainable Development Goal. The game uses wearable gloves with accelerometer and gyroscope sensors for hand posture recognition, processed via sensor fusion and a feedforward neural network (FNN). Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) with a 4-to-1 Central and Peripheral architecture facilitates communication, while the neural network function runs on the BLE microcontroller. The system development includes hardware, algorithms, and Unity game software implementation.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Palmprint Detection Using Different YOLO Models
abstract: As biometric technology increasingly integrates into identity verification and security, palmprint recognition showcases significant potential due to its uniqueness, stability, and non-invasiveness. However, the accuracy and efficiency of this recognition method are heavily reliant on the precise localization and extraction of the ROI within the palmprint. This study investigates the application of the latest versions of the YOLO object detection algorithm in palmprint ROI detection and their effects on authentication system performance. The research results indicate that YOLOv9, YOLOv10, and YOLOv11 all performed excellently in terms of mAP and F1 metrics, with only minor differences among them. Yet, YOLOv9 achieved an accuracy rate of 94.44% in comprehensive evaluations, surpassing the other two generations. This result underscores the effectiveness of YOLOv9 in palmprint ROI detection and provides valuable empirical support for the optimization and application of YOLO algorithms in the field of biometric recognition.

articleTitle: FitMirror: An Artificial Intelligence Mirror System for Elderly Physical Fitness Diagnosis
abstract: This paper proposes a mirror-based artificial intelligence physical fitness motion detection system, called FitMirror, designed for assessing the physical fitness of the elderly. In addition to assisting fitness coaches or physical therapists in automatically tracking the number of movements completed by the elderly during fitness exercises, FitMirror can also identify the angle changes between joints in each fitness movement. Experimental results demonstrate that FitMirror effectively recognizes and evaluates fitness activities, making it a reliable tool for diagnosing the fitness levels of the elderly in fitness centers or rehabilitation institutions.

articleTitle: A Novel Flexibility Analyses for Yoga Pose Difficulty Evaluation by Body Joint Points Based Angle Estimation
abstract: In this study, a novel method to evaluate the execution difficulty of yoga poses is developed based on body flexibility by focusing on analyzing specific key body joint angles. To enhance the accuracy of yoga pose difficulty assessment, the datasets of yoga poses are divided into the front-facing and side-facing parts, with unique calculation methods applied for each perspective. In the proposed analysis method, the selected body joint points based angle estimation are used to detect whether the body is bending forward or backward, and it enables precise flexibility measurements. This study was based on nearly 100 images of yoga poses by covering 5 yoga poses with different difficulty levels. Experimental results show that the proposed method has an accuracy of 83% in the yoga poses difficulty evaluations, which is 6% higher than the existing methods. This approach not only provides a more comprehensive yoga pose difficulty evaluation framework but also helps users better understand their flexibility levels and pose difficulty during doing yoga self-practice.

articleTitle: An Environmentally Friendly Fishing Android-Based Mobile Device App for Penghu Islands (Pescadores), Taiwan
abstract: Penghu Islands (Pescadores), Taiwan's outlying islands surrounded by the sea, boast rich fishing resources that attract many anglers. However, successful fishing requires more than just gear: it involves understanding the varying fish species available in different locations, times, and climates, as well as adhering to relevant laws and regulations. To address these needs, this paper proposes an environmentally friendly fishing Android-based mobile device App specifically for the Penghu Islands. The proposed Android-based mobile device App aims to gather essential information, including local fishing regulations, aquatic safety tips, and important precautions. Its goal is to equip fishermen with the resources necessary to fish successfully and with peace of mind.

articleTitle: Speech Abusive Language Detection System Using MFCC Speech Feature Extraction and Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: As bullying rapidly spreads in schools, many parents are becoming increasingly concerned about their children being subjected to bullying by peers, which could negatively impact their physical and mental health. This paper proposes an abusive language detection system that combines Mel-frequency Cepstrum Coefficients (MFCC) speech features with a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). Audio files which contain daily abusive phrases in the Minnan dialect are initially preprocesses to eliminate non-speech interference. Subsequently, the MFCC algorithm is applied to extract speech features that closely capture auditory characteristics. The CNN classification model is trained to learn the MFCC features and classify the phrases into their respective categories. Experimental results indicate that the CNN model achieves an average recognition accuracy of 91.9%. Finally, the CNN model was deployed on an embedded platform, where it achieves an average recognition time of 0.54 seconds per phrase and an average recognition accuracy of 86.25%.

articleTitle: Effectiveness Investigation of Drawing Exactness Assessment Method in Portrait Drawing Learning Assistant System
abstract: Portrait drawing is important for developing drawing skills and humanistic sensibilities. It is challenging for novices to draw portraits because it is difficult to master facial proportions and structures without professional guidance. For this reason, we developed a Portrait Drawing Learning Assist System (PDLAS) to help novices by providing auxiliary lines for facial features using OpenPose and OpenCV. Novices can use these auxiliary lines to draw portraits on the iPad. To improve the feedback, we implemented an evaluation method using the local Normalized Cross-Correlation (NCC) algorithm, which calculates similarity scores between the original face photo and the drawing image. It focuses on specific regions such as the eyes, nose, mouth, eyebrows, and hair. In this paper, we asked 3 students at Okayama University in Japan to use PDLAS to draw portraits for evaluation. We prompted users to refine low-scoring facial features and reevaluate to observe improvements in their overall scores.

articleTitle: Anonymous-Diffusion: Blockchain-Based Privacy-Preserving Stable Diffusion
abstract: The field of generative AI is currently seeing a surge in text-to-image generation. Among open-source projects, Stable Diffusion stands out as the state-of-the-art. Artists and service providers often customize diffusion models for unique textures. However, there is a lack of privacy protection for users' input text prompts, output images, and customized models on servers. Ensuring privacy is essential for user trust and safeguarding intellectual property. Current privacy-preserving diffusion models rely on fully homomorphic encryption (FHE), which is time-intensive and can compromise image quality. We introduce Anonymous-Diffusion, a diffusion as a service (DAAS) framework. This framework maintains privacy without using FHE by exploiting the irreversible nature of neural network layers and the characteristic that predicted noise in the diffusion process follows a normalized Gaussian distribution. Furthermore, we ensure anonymity by Smart Contract and Blockchain. User can use this service on demand anonymously. In comparison to existing research like HE-diffusion, which incurs a 200% time overhead and noticeable quality degradation, our protocol achieves the same level of security with only a 4% time overhead and no loss in image quality. To our knowledge, this is the first solution to achieve these results without FHE while preserving high-quality image output.

articleTitle: A 20-Gb/s 1.4-pJ/bit Wireline Transceiver for Chip-to-Chip Interfaces in 40-nm CMOS
abstract: The paper demonstrates a 20-Gb/s transceiver for chip-to-chip communication over silicon interposer. The PLL generates a 20-GHz clock for the transmitter to drive data and for the receiver to recover the clock through the timing recovery loop. Because of the low signal swing, the power compared to regular rail-to-rail CMOS driver is less for the transmitter. The phase-interpolating technique is employed for the clock recovery of the receiver. Implemented in 40-nm CMOS process, the transceiver operates on a 1V supply and demonstrates a power efficiency of 1.4 pJ/bit.

articleTitle: File-Level EC : A Chunk Containing Meaning
abstract: In recent years, with the widespread use of mobile devices such as smartphones laptop PCs etc., the amounts of data exchanged over the internet has been increasing. Erasure Coding (EC) which offers excellent storage efficiency is well-suited for protecting large amounts of data. Meanwhile, if the required number of chunks for restoration is not available, the remaining data chunks are wasted. So, we propose File-Level EC (FEC) which enables partial data recovery by mapping files to data chunks. However, it remains as challenges to implement FEC in storage software and verify practical performance. Specifically, FEC needs to be integrated into a storage software, and its overhead compared to conventional EC is quantitatively evaluated. In this paper, we describe the implementation of FEC for MinIO and evaluate its performance. We evaluated the throughput during data transfer using the MinIO client and the encoding processing time within the MinIO server. We confirmed that FEC has an overhead of within 20% compared to conventional EC, which is within a sufficiently practical range. We concluded that FEC is an effective method applicable in real-world operational environments by the evaluation.

articleTitle: Fundamental Study on Relationship between High-Frequency Magnetic and Mechanical Properties of Soft Magnetic Composites and Chemical Structure of Insulation Polymer Treated under Various Annealing Conditions
abstract: This study investigated the high-frequency magnetic properties under 1 MHz and 3 mT, as well as the mechanical characteristics of soft magnetic composites and the chemical structure of the insulation polymer treated under various annealing conditions. Among the iron particles comprising the soft magnetic composites, Fe-6.5Si powder and dimethylpolysiloxane were utilized as the soft magnetic powder and insulation polymer, respectively. The organic components of the insulating resin in the composites heat-treated at temperatures above 673 K degraded; however, the degradation of inorganic components was not observed under infrared spectroscopy even at 873 K. Although the composite underwent moderate mechanical deterioration due to the structural change of the resin from heat treatment, the electrical resistivity of the composite heat-treated at 873 K was reduced to 1/100th of that of the composite heat-treated at 573 K. Despite the significant reduction in electrical resistivity, the core loss did not increase under the given excitation conditions.

articleTitle: A Fully Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Routing Method for 3D-Torus Network-on-Chips
abstract: For developing dependable and high-performance processors which are key components in consumer systems and services, this paper proposes a fully adaptive fault-tolerant routing method for three-dimensional (3D) torus Network-on-Chips (NoCs). In contrast to existing methods, the proposed method allows to take minimal paths for any pairs of source and destination nodes by not only detouring faulty regions but also passing through them. Simulation results show that the proposed method reduces average communication latency by up to 30.6% with eight less virtual channels.

articleTitle: Amphibious Robot with Horizontal Articulated Mechanism
abstract: In recent years, the frequency of heavy rainfall disasters in Japan has increased due to the intensification of climate change-induced phenomena, accompanied by frequent occurrences of secondary disasters such as floods and landslides. Amphibious robots capable of mobility both on land and water surfaces are gaining attention for their potential to enable movement in environments that are challenging for humans to access, particularly for lifesaving and information-gathering during heavy rainfall disasters. In this paper, we develop a robot of amphibious with a horizontal articulated mechanism capable of moving on both land and water surface, with a focus on activities expected during heavy rainfall disasters. The proposed robot has a cylindrical torso, legs with horizontal articulation mechanisms, and a drive system powered by a single actuator. The experimental results confirmed that stable movement can be achieved on both land and water surface.

articleTitle: Beam Training for Partially-Connected Structure in XL-MIMO Systems with Spatial Non-Stationarity
abstract: This paper presents a beam training for XL-MIMO systems operating in near-field non-stationary channels with a partially-connected architecture. The proposed method accounts for the spatial non-stationarity by selecting distinct beamforming codewords for each subarray, which are tailored to the different channels experienced by individual antenna parts. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed beam training scheme outperforms conventional techniques in all SNR ranges, offering improved beamforming performance and better adaptation to the near-field and non-stationary environments of XL-MIMO channels.

articleTitle: Leveraging Human-Machine Interaction to Optimize Sustainability with Big Data and AI Technologies
abstract: Human-machine interaction is becoming more important in modern technology, especially in improving organizational performance and sustainability with the help of artificial intelligence and big data analytics. The purpose of this study is to examine the role of big data analytics and artificial intelligence in the enhancement of sustainable performance via the mediation of sustainable process integration strategies. This research gathers data from managers within Taiwan's manufacturing industry by employing a cluster sampling method. According to the results, big data analytics and artificial intelligence had positive significant associations with sustainable performance and sustainable process integration. Likewise, sustainable process integration significantly impacted sustainable performance. Furthermore, in terms of indirect impact, big data analytics and artificial intelligence had a substantial indirect association with sustainable performance by having sustainable process integration as the mediating variable.

Author Keywords: Big Data Analytics And Artificial Intelligence
Partial Least Square - Structural Equation Model

articleTitle: An Adaptive Low-Complexity Compression Algorithm for Vehicle Systems
abstract: Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) are increasingly integrated into modern vehicles, relying on high-speed image transmission from on-board cameras to control systems. This study presents an adaptive lossless image compression algorithm designed to reduce transmission data while maintaining high image quality. By dynamically switching between Color Filter Array (CFA) compression and predictive compression, the proposed method achieves an average compression rate of 3.835 and a Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) of 30.57 dB, significant improvements in efficiency, making it suitable for automotive applications.

articleTitle: A New Priority Forwarding Method for Emergency Massages Using Multiple Sending Queues on NDN-VANET
abstract: VANET (Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networking) is well-known, evolving network that connects a wide variety of devices, including automobiles and infrastructure related to motorized society. However, due to the dynamic topology, achieving stable communication remains a significant challenge. To address this issue, NDN-VANET, which employs the Named Data Networking (NDN) mechanism to enhance message delivery performance through network caching, has been proposed. Implementing NDN functionality in VANET enables stable data dissemination, even under unreliable wireless links. However, for emergency data dissemination, NDN-VANET still faces issues, as NDN lacks a mechanism to prioritize emergency data over regular data. The proposed method in this paper prioritizes emergency data by multiple sending queues at a RSU (Road Side Unit), based on the significance of each Data. The evaluation results demonstrate that the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Packet Allocation: Improving the Accuracy of Mobile Device Count Estimation
abstract: This study specifically examines development of a method for estimating the number of mobile devices in dense smoke environments that arise because of tunnel fire accidents, with the aim of facilitating evacuation. Various sensing technologies such as radio wave positioning and image processing have been used with inflow analysis systems, but their applicability in environments with poor visibility and confined spaces, such as smoke-filled tunnels, remains limited. To address this shortcoming, we propose a method using Wi-Fi probe requests for estimation of the number of mobile devices. Prior research has demonstrated that dense smoke exerts only minimal effects of on radio wave characteristics in such environments. Building on these earlier findings, we apply principal component analysis to reduce the dimensionality of features extracted from Wi-Fi probe requests and subsequently apply cluster analysis to estimate the number of devices. To enhance the estimation accuracy of our proposed method, we introduce a novel packet data allocation technique based on data collected from multiple Wi-Fi packet captures deployed within a tunnel environment. Then we validate the accuracy of this allocation technique and report the effectiveness of our proposed method for estimating the number of mobile devices.

articleTitle: An Analog-Based Phase Shedding Control Technique for Interleaved Boost PFC Converters
abstract: This paper proposes an efficient phase shedding control (PSC) technique for interleaved boost PFC converters (IB-PFC), which can be implemented using a simple analog circuit. A comprehensive mathematical loss model is presented to properly calculate the optimal phase switching point, complemented by a detailed explanation of the operating principle and design methodology of the analog circuit in use. The experimental validation using a 2.5 kW converter prototype with the UCC28070A controller indicates that the proposed PSC technique enhances the efficiency by approximately 1% at a power level of 10% load. Besides, the optimal phase-changing point is identified to occur at around 35% of the rated load, effectively improving the performance under light-to-moderate load conditions.

articleTitle: ECG Signal Classification Using 1D ResNet-18 with Integrated CBAM and Auxiliary Classifier
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) classification is essential for the early diagnosis of heart diseases. In this study, we propose an enhanced method using a one-dimensional ResNet-18 model combined with a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) and an auxiliary classifier, both commonly applied in computer vision tasks, to process 1D ECG data. To address class imbalance, we applied ADASYN for data balancing and implemented data augmentation techniques on the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database.
